curriculum.lesson_evidence: Natural hazards in Australia include bushfires, floods, storms and cyclones in some regions. Hazards become disasters when they harm people and places; risk depends on location and preparation.

lesson.child_mission: Natural hazards in Australia include bushfires, floods, storms and cyclones in some regions. Hazards become disasters when they harm people and places; risk depends on location and preparation.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Which hazard is more associated with dry, vegetated landscapes in hot windy weather: flood or bushfire?

FEEDBACK
Bushfire.

WATCH FOR
Assuming every hazard hits every town equally ignores geography.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Complete a hazards table for bushfire, flood and severe storm: conditions, likely regions, one effect. Cite a published emergency/education source.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.

teach_steps.explain:
Natural hazards in Australia include bushfires, floods, storms and cyclones in some regions. Hazards become disasters when they harm people and places; risk depends on location and preparation.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on sources, places and respectful community knowledge, rather than guessing from a single picture. Keep every claim linked to evidence.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the sources, map features or community examples that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your record with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your evidence? If a detail is uncertain, identify what source you would need next. One deliberate, evidence-based revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
